rationale: The agent verified identity using full name and zip, matched to a single user, and inspected the user’s orders to identify the two tablets. When the user asked to return the more expensive (gold) tablet and refund to credit card, the agent initially stated the refund would go to the credit card, but upon the user’s follow-up question, correctly checked/relied on the order’s payment history and explained that refunds must go to the original method for that order (a gift card) or to an existing gift card. The user then explicitly authorized proceeding with a return and refund to the gift card. The agent executed the return on the correct order and item, with the correct refund destination, and provided accurate final details (item, amount, gift card). The action was performed only after explicit confirmation. Minor issue: the agent prematurely promised a credit-card refund before confirming eligibility; however, they corrected this before making any changes and the final information and action were correct. Overall, it meets the pass bar.
